name: INBO Botox

card.summary: A Korean botulinum toxin type A brand, marketed in Thailand and Asia, used to smooth frown and forehead lines and slim the jaw by relaxing targeted muscles.
card.note: Prescription injectable given by clinicians; marketing claims on clinic sites are promotional.

quick.overview:
inBo is a botulinum toxin type A product described by Thai clinics as a Korean toxin made from the Swedish CCUG 7968 strain. Botulinum toxin temporarily relaxes injected muscles, which softens expression lines such as crow's feet, forehead lines and frown lines, and can slim the jaw when the masseter is treated.
Clinics report results within 1 to 2 days and typically 4 to 6 months of effect. These figures come from a clinic article, not from independent trials.
quick.how: It is a clinic procedure: a trained practitioner injects the product into chosen muscles, and treatments are repeated when the effect wears off. Areas listed by clinics include crow's feet, forehead, frown lines, jawline, neck, masseters and areas of excess sweating.
quick.risks: Botulinum toxin products in general can cause bruising, headache, drooping eyelid or brow and unintended weakness of nearby muscles. It is a prescription product, and whether the "inBo" clinic brand is the same as the manufacturer's INIBO is not clear from available pages.

lead: inBo (also INIBO) is a brand of botulinum toxin type A sold in Korea and marketed by clinics in Thailand and elsewhere in Asia. A Bangkok clinic article describes it as made from Clostridium botulinum strain CCUG 7968, developed by the Culture Collection University of Gothenburg, Sweden. [1]

People use botulinum toxin to reduce dynamic wrinkles and to slim the lower face by treating the masseter muscle. The clinic lists crow's feet, forehead lines, frown lines, jawline and neckline, masseter reduction and excess sweating as treatment areas, with results in 1 to 2 days and a duration of 4 to 6 months. [1]

The clinic article claims 99.99% purity, narrow diffusion and lower resistance risk, and cites Thai FDA and KFDA approval; these are the clinic's own claims. [1] For botulinum toxin in general, Botox Cosmetic was approved by the FDA in 2002 for glabellar lines. [2]

chain: Toxin blocks signals to injected muscle
Smoother lines or slimmer jaw contour
angle.text: Injected into expression muscles, botulinum toxin softens lines such as frown and forehead creases. When used on the masseter, clinics describe a slimmer lower-face contour.

paras: The clinic article describes inBo as the first and only brand in Thailand to use the CCUG 7968 strain and lists Thai FDA and KFDA approval. [1] The manufacturer INIBIO describes INIBO as indicated for temporary improvement of moderate to severe glabellar lines in adults aged 18 to 65. Some clinic descriptions of "inBo" and manufacturer materials for "INIBO" may refer to the same product, though available pages do not settle this.

Cosmetic botulinum toxin typically works on wrinkles in the upper third of the face. Wrinkle smoothing is usually visible 3 to 5 days after injection, with the maximum about a week later, and effects on glabellar lines typically last 2 to 4 months, sometimes up to 6 or more depending on the product. [2] The inBo clinic quotes faster onset and longer duration. [1]

General botulinum toxin side effects include unintended weakness of facial muscles, headache, flu-like symptoms, drooping eyelid or brow, double vision in rare reports and bruising lasting 7 to 11 days in some cases. [2]
No studies have been found for the inBo brand. Botulinum toxin type A in general has extensive trial data and regulatory approvals. [2]
